views.visibleScope: Move effect behavior and implementation claims; not a Chroma visual reference.
Normal and proposed plain/HSL slider states.

registryScope.notes: The registry query reports 91 slider declarations; Color-specific functional gradients are at chromasmith-22.html:1992-1994 and 2042-2044.

visibleObservations.fact: The visible labels, tabular values, focus ring, and native range input are separate from the SVG silhouette.
The prototype exposes normal and proposed controls side by side and can immediately hide the decorative SVG layer.

repositoryEvidence.claim: The existing slider component contract is proposed and describes continuous tonal and colour adjustment with a visible value.
The component registry identifies 91 slider declarations, including Color functional-gradient declarations #sl-hsl-h/#sl-hsl-s/#sl-hsl-l.
Existing .fx-slider uses a 16px visual control and mobile rules raise its interactive height; the prototype preserves a 44px range hit area without increasing the 3px visible track.
Existing .fx-slider-grad supplies the functional HSL gradient and a 16px round thumb.
At the audited source commit, liquid-gooey separates a filtered SVG silhouette below from unfiltered interactive content above.
At the audited source commit, move uses a trailing satellite and motion observation; reduced motion snaps immediately and source cleanup cancels rAF/disconnects observers.

missing.state: focused browser evidence of continuous drag

applicableDesignRules.rule: Motion is restrained and short; nothing bounces or auto-plays.
Focus uses a 2px ring at a 2px offset and the minimum hit target is 44px.
Use the existing Mist Blue/Slate Blue action colour by theme; do not introduce a decorative accent.

proposedInterpretations.statement: Apply the effect only as an optional SVG silhouette beneath a native range input, never to labels, values, focus indicators, or HSL gradient pixels.
Start with trail 0.28, SVG blur 3px, no wobble, and a 180ms damped settle; these are deliberately more restrained than the library defaults.
If SVG filters, feature detection, or a required browser behavior is unavailable, hide the surface immediately and retain the normal Chroma slider unchanged.

userDecisions.decision: Evaluate an isolated Color-slider prototype; do not migrate Chroma to React or production implementation.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Keep or reject the effect after review?
Apply to plain sliders, functional-gradient sliders, or both?
Show it only while dragging or also during settling?

geometrySpacing.statement: Keep the visible 3px track and 16px thumb geometry; put the real range in a 44px row-local interaction area.

typography.statement: Preserve Chroma’s SF Pro Text stack, existing label treatment, and tabular numeric value styling.

colorsContrastRoles.statement: Use current dark/light Chroma tokens and preserve functional HSL gradients; the liquid uses the existing action token only.

motionInteraction.statement: Decorative movement follows input changes, stops its rAF after settling, and is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

responsiveBehavior.statement: At narrow width, comparison panels stack; each slider remains row-bounded with no clipping or layout shift.

accessibility.statement: The native range owns keyboard handling, focus, ARIA name, value behavior, and pointer hit target; SVG is aria-hidden and pointer-events:none.

targets.statement: Future production work, if approved, binds to the slider contract and Color declarations identified by the registry; this prototype touches no production target.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Default, changed, dragging, keyboard-focus, disabled, reduced-motion, light, dark, and mobile-width states retain labels/values without blur or layout shift.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Focused browser screenshots and keyboard checks.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: No effect overlaps, clips, or moves outside its slider row; the 44px target remains usable.
Missing SVG filter support immediately renders the normal slider with no behavior regression.
Native range input remains the real accessible control.

evidence.statement: Use equal-size captures for reference:compare as pixel-difference evidence only; run Chromium and Playwright WebKit when available and record browser uncertainty rather than infer Safari support.
